overview.headline: Population genetics and variation in human groups

keyPoints.point: Population genetics tracks distribution and change in allele frequencies under evolutionary forces
keyPoints.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies

keyPoints.point: Evolutionary pressures named are natural selection, genetic drift, mutation and migration
keyPoints.quote: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration.

keyPoints.point: Biology defines population as group whose members breed primarily among themselves with isolation
keyPoints.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves.

keyPoints.point: Racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of genetic variation distribution in human species
keyPoints.quote: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation in the human species.

keyTerms.gloss: study of distribution and change in allele frequencies in populations
keyTerms.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies

keyTerms.gloss: estimates describing variant occurrence within population groups
keyTerms.quote: each is used to provide estimates of allele frequencies.

keyTerms.gloss: genetic change from random sampling in populations under drift forces
keyTerms.quote: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration.

keyTerms.gloss: evolutionary pressure where advantageous traits persist through selection
keyTerms.quote: under the influence of the four evolutionary forces: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration.

keyTerms.gloss: alternative grouping by shared origin used when race classification is inadequate
keyTerms.quote: An alternative to classifying the human species by race is to divide them by ethnicity.
